say: Your car's engine sets off thousands of tiny explosions every single minute. On purpose. And somehow, that's how you get to the taco place.
Inside are cylinders. Each one has a piston, a metal plug that slides up and down, kind of like the inside of a syringe.
Step one: suck. The piston slides down, a valve opens, and a mist of air and fuel gets pulled in.
Step two: squeeze. The valve shuts, and the piston pushes back up, crushing that mist into a tiny space.
Step three: bang. The spark plug fires, the fuel burns in a flash, and the hot gas slams the piston down. This is the only step that makes power.
Step four: blow. The piston comes back up and pushes the burnt gas out through the exhaust. Suck, squeeze, bang, blow.
But a piston only goes up and down, and wheels need to spin. So it's linked to a crankshaft, which turns that pumping into spinning, like your legs on bike pedals.
Each cylinder fires once every two turns. So a four cylinder engine at two thousand RPM fires about four thousand times a minute. That's around sixty six bangs a second.
That spin goes through the gearbox, down to the wheels, and off you go. Thousands of tiny fires, one smooth ride.
